text:
Aisha (People Ops): Quick heads-up — temporary Q2 exception to PTO carryover + an update to travel pre-approval process. Please read and share with your teams. 

Aisha (People Ops): TL;DR: For Q2 only, employees with caregiving responsibilities can carry over up to an extra 24 hours of PTO (on top of standard cap) if they submit the short exception form by 2026-05-15. Also: travel preapproval for non-emergency international trips now requires a one‑click finance code (TRVL-Q2) on the travel form. 

Jonah Rivera: Thanks Aisha — can managers approve retroactively for trips that already happened in April? 

Aisha (People Ops): Jonah — short answer: yes for PTO exceptions if the time-off was used in Apr/May and the form is filed by 5/15. For travel, retroactive corporate-card coding to TRVL-Q2 is allowed only if finance confirms charges; include the original receipt when you submit. 

Priya K: For our London folks on local contracts, does carryover impact tax/holiday rules? Who do they ping? 

Aisha (People Ops): Priya — good catch. Carryover itself is a payroll input (we're not changing local statutory holiday rules). International assignees & local hires should cc payroll@redwood.com when submitting the exception form so payroll can confirm tax/treatment. We included a step in the form to flag "local contract". 

Evan M: Is sabbatical accrual affected? I have someone starting sabbatical in July. 

Aisha (People Ops): Evan — no change to sabbatical accruals or eligibility. This Q2 exception only affects up to 24h PTO carryover and only for caregivers. Sabbatical rules unchanged. 

Priya K: Can you paste the form fields? Quick copy is easier for managers. 

Aisha (People Ops): Sure — form link: https://intranet.redwood.com/forms/pto-q2-exception. Fields (short): 
```
- Employee name 
- Manager name 
- Team/location 
- Reason (select: caregiving / medical / other) 
- Dates of time off claimed for exception 
- Attach supporting doc (optional) 
- Payroll cc (checkbox for international/local contract) 
- Manager approval checkbox + signature field 
```

Aisha (People Ops): For travel preapproval: when creating travel request, add finance code TRVL-Q2 in the "Expense code" dropdown, and attach itinerary + corporate card receipt if already charged. This flags the trip for expedited review. 

Jonah Rivera: Will People Ops/Finance run a report of approvals so managers don't have to chase? 

Aisha (People Ops): Yes — PeopleOpsBot will DM managers weekly with pending exceptions and finance will provide a summary to managers and regional directors on 2026-05-20. PeopleOpsBot: Reminder scheduled: every Monday at 09:00 (for managers with pending forms). 

PeopleOpsBot: Automated reminder queued for 2026-05-04 — sending to managers with >0 pending PTO exception requests. 

Evan M: Any guidance for public-facing comms? Our team needs to update customer-facing docs for travel-coded work trips. 

Aisha (People Ops): Not strictly necessary. If an update touches billing or customer invoices (e.g., travel billed to clients), loop in Finance and Legal. Otherwise internal process only. 

Jonah Rivera: Thanks — one more: if manager denies an exception, is there an appeal path? 

Aisha (People Ops): Yes — denied exceptions auto-create an appeal ticket to People Ops that the employee can request within 7 days. Managers should include reason in the form. Appeal goes to People Ops + HRBP for final review. 

Aisha (People Ops): Final note: this is time-limited for Q2 only to help teams with seasonally higher caregiver load. We will reassess for Q3 based on usage & finance impact. If you have edge cases or need support with process changes, ping me or open a ticket at https://intranet.redwood.com/people-ops/tickets. :sparkles: 

Priya K: Appreciated. Will relay to EMEA managers. 

Jonah Rivera: Copy — I'll add to our weekly manager sync agenda. :thumbsup: 

Aisha (People Ops): Thank you everyone.
